findings.text: follow-on: the figure and both fragments state the reclaimed branch refuses in both readers and that the classifier and the obligations duty reader take the same branch, but reckon/crew/obligations.py:708 calls newest_review_for_headless_run with reclaimed=False, so for a run that named a worktree no longer on disk the duty reader reads the store's newest record rather than refusing; the new case's vanished-tree assertion depends on exactly that, so the artifact's claim that both readers take one branch overstates the agreement.

follow-on: the repair arms include the real-store inventory test tests/test_member_friction.py, whose collection/setup error id shifts between the base and head arms under concurrent fleet writes; the store's own read-time annotation counts the head arm's error id as an added failure, so this review reads a total capped at 5 rather than its scored 84 until the id is retired by name, and the run's failure_attribution names only the file rather than the full node id.

The two arms share the same seven FAILED ids (all tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py) and carry one ERROR id each, a different one, so the reviewed run's own derivation reads tests/test_member_friction.py::test_member_dispatch_without_a_registered_checkout_names_repo as added and added_failure_count is 1.

item_verdicts.manifest: The reviewed run's manifest.md reads status complete with its four commits, both suite records carrying literal commands, revisions and failure ids, a bare negative_control_log path, and measurement_module/measurement_cwd for the scratch base arm; its scope_note discloses that the live pointer still records the original dispatch's write paths, which the coordinator owns, rather than hiding it.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The six delta paths (reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/crew/obligations.py, tests/test_reclaimed_run_review_head.py, both evidence fragments, the figure directory) all sit inside the repair brief's declared write scope in resume-1-advice.txt; nothing outside it is changed and the plan is not edited from the worktree.

justifications.durability: test_a_live_run_with_no_readable_tree_still_owes_its_sub_floor_duty asserts the duty for a vanished worktree and for a nameless tree, and the negative control reverses the two source files to redden it on an empty duty set; unwatched, reckon/cli.py:4944 still passes an empty head for a live pointer with no readable tree, so the disposition CLI keeps the lost-review shape the repair fixed for the duty reader.
justifications.evidence: the arms over fourteen gate files are recorded at logs/repair-baseline-arm.log (7 failed, 111 passed, 1 error, EXIT=1 at 0fc262e3f) and logs/repair-arm-2.log (7 failed, 112 passed, 1 error, EXIT=1 at d69cf81f), the negative control at logs/negative-control-repair.log reddens the new case on an empty duty set (1 failed, 2 deselected, EXIT=1), and logs/store-inventory-alone.log clears the error (5 passed, EXIT=0); but the arms include a real-store test whose error id shifts between arms, so the run's own derivation reads it as an added failure.
justifications.fit: newest_review_for_headless_run is named by the mechanism it carries, the docstrings state the branch and the reason, no added name carries a plan label, and the decision-tree figure has no data-ink violation.
justifications.goal_fidelity: finding f49b6b9881f named the duty reader losing its duty over an empty head, and the repair answers it in one function both readers now take, with the classifier's reclaimed refusal preserved at reckon/crew/recovery.py:699.
